text:
Carolina was up two goals before the game was three and a half minutes old, and for most of the next hour that lead looked like a loan. Logan Stankoven scored 57 seconds in, Jesperi Kotkaniemi deflected one home at 3:20, and then the Islanders spent the second period calmly collecting what they were owed.

Mitchell Chaffee tipped one in at 3:40 of the second, with Matthew Schaefer and Casey Cizikas assisting, and Brayden Schenn tied it two minutes later on a wraparound. Andrei Svechnikov answered within a minute on a backhand set up by Sebastian Aho and William Carrier, but Victor Eklund's slap shot at 17:13 made it 3-3. That goal took New York from a 29% chance of winning to 52%.

It was that kind of night: level in almost every way that counts. Expected goals, the quality of each side's chances, finished 3.50 to 3.45 for Carolina. Shot attempts went 64 to 63. Replay every shot and the Islanders win 52% of the time. Brandon Bussi's best moment came with the score tied in the third, when he stopped Simon Holmstrom on a 37% look, the best chance of the night that didn't go in.

Then the same three Hurricanes struck again. At 14:52 of the third Carrier buried a backhand off a 36% chance, with Svechnikov and Aho on the assists, and Carolina's win chance jumped from 48% to 86%. Svechnikov was the engine all night: seven shots on goal, and 1.89 expected goals for against 0.55 against while he was on the ice. Carrier, a second-round pick of the Blues back in 2013, finished as the first star with a goal and an assist in 13:54. Jalen Chatfield added the fifth at 19:09.

The Islanders will look at two things. Their power play went 0 for 4 and produced 0.47 expected goals, and their goaltending came up a little short in a game with no room for it: Semyon Varlamov faced 38 shots and allowed 0.65 goals more than expected, while Bussi saw 27 and saved 0.45 more. New York won 40 of 61 faceoffs and outhit Carolina 26 to 16. It just didn't win the one shot that mattered.
headline: Carrier's backhand settles a game Carolina kept giving back
